guides.summary: Which apps and services your agent can work with, grouped by job, and where to connect each one.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: Archie reaches each of these from this computer, on your own account where there is one. Archie Mobile is the one that goes through our servers, locked so we cannot read it. What your agent reads goes to the AI company that answers you, as the guide called Where your information goes explains.
Mail and calendar

items: Gmail and Google Calendar.
Outlook mail and calendar: Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live, or a work or school account.

iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, AOL, Zoho Mail, and GMX, with an app password you make on that provider's website: mail, plus the calendar where the provider has one. These have not yet been tried on a real account.

body.text: Connect them on your agent's Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files. Email features need an AI account of your own: they do not run on the free trial's credits or a plan with the AI included.
Files

items: Google Drive, but only the Sheets and Docs you pick in Google's own picker.
Files you add on your agent's Knowledge tab, which stay on this computer.
A file attached to an email your agent reads.

body.text: To-do lists and meetings

items: Todoist, and Google Tasks through a Google account.
Fireflies, the meeting recorder.
Zoom recordings saved on this computer. Archie has no connection to a Zoom account.

body.text: Chat apps

items: Telegram, Discord, Slack, and Matrix.
iMessage, on a Mac only. Windows has no iMessage.
Archie Mobile, our own phone app: from the App Store on iPhone, or as a download on Android. It needs a plan or a free trial.

body.text: Pick one on your agent's Setup tab, under Chat app. With none, your agent answers in the Archie window.
Business tools

Follow Up Boss connects with a key. In Follow Up Boss, open Admin, then API, press Create API Key, and paste the key on the Connections tab, under Apps. Then ask your agent to bring in your people, deals, or tasks. They come in on a card you look over, nothing is added to your lists until you press Add, and nothing in Follow Up Boss is changed. GoHighLevel connects directly. Make a token for it in your GoHighLevel sub-account's Settings, under Private Integrations, and paste it on the Connections tab, under Apps.
Square, Acuity Scheduling, and Instagram posts through Zernio are in the store, and have not yet been tried on a real account. Neither has Follow Up Boss.
Texting

Texting works only on a Mac, through its Messages app; Windows has no texting. The Text Replies add-on reads the texts that arrive there and writes a reply to each one that needs it, and nothing goes out until you press Send. It needs an AI account of your own, so it does not run on the free trial's credits or a plan with the AI included. Phone calls are a switch of their own: with Call businesses on, on the Setup tab under What it can do, your agent can phone a business on your own Bland account, after you press Place the call.
Lights at home
Your agent can switch Philips Hue, WiZ and LIFX lights and plugs on your own wifi, once you add each one on the Connections tab, under Home devices. These have not yet been tried with real lights.
Websites and apps

For a website with no connection of its own, Computer control lets your agent open the site and use it itself, on a Mac or Windows, and on a Mac the apps you allow. It is off until you turn it on, on the Connections tab, under Computer control.
Something not on the list

The Apps list on the Connections tab has more, with a search box. Most of those were built from each company's published instructions and have not yet been tried on a real account. For an app that is not there, press Something else, give it a name, the web address of its API and the key that app gave you, then write a skill that uses it. This works only with an app that hands out a key.
If something here does not work the first time, write to questions@otianai.com and say which one.

guides.title: What your agent costs to run
guides.summary: Who you pay, what costs more, and how to cap it.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: You pay the AI company directly

Your agent uses a key to your own AI account, and every reply is charged there at that company’s prices. Nothing routes through us, which is also why we can’t see what you say to it. One catch: web searches run on your AI company’s own computers and are billed to your key, so the search text reaches them. Still not us.
What each thing costs

items: An ordinary reply: a fraction of a cent.

A look-up with the Researcher skill: about 10 cents, the searches and the pages they bring back included, with at most five searches per task on Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI. Groq charges per search but sets its own number, so it has no cap. Gemini, DeepSeek, and Mistral have no live search.
A Deep Research run: about 40 cents, with up to twenty searches.
A routine: the same as asking yourself.
A long document costs more, because it goes in with the question.

body.text: A routine every 15 minutes runs 96 times a day. Pick the slowest schedule that still tells you in time.
Set a monthly limit
Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI let you cap a key’s monthly spend, in about a minute. Groq and Gemini have no such cap, and Groq needs billing on before Archie works, so check its limits at setup.

items: Open your provider’s console and find billing or limits.
Set a monthly cap you’d be fine seeing on a statement.
Set the warning lower, so you hear before you hit it.

body.text: In Archie, the Account page’s Spending section shows what your agents spent per AI account.
If a bill surprises you

Check routines and Email Manager first: they spend with nobody watching. Turn a routine off with the switch on its skill’s card. For Email Manager, open its row on the Skills tab and set Tell me about at most … emails an hour.

guides.title: What your agent will never do
guides.summary: What your agent cannot do, and the limit in Archie that stops each one.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: Apart from the one about payment instructions, these are limits in Archie itself, so they hold whichever AI company you connect and whatever anybody types at it.
No conversations with other AIs

The only conversation your agent is in is the one with you. It can hand one job to a helper, such as a researcher, and read the answer; that helper cannot pass the job on. There is no group of AIs and nowhere for them to post.
Idle until something starts it
Three things start your agent: you writing to it, a time you set, and a check of a mailbox you connected. Quitting Archie stops all three, and so does the computer going to sleep.
No commands or scripts

Your agent cannot run a command or a script on this computer. It has a fixed list of actions, like reading a file you added or writing a draft. The only code it writes is a short Python program it runs inside Archie on a Mac, with no internet, seeing only copies of files you gave it, and the program is under its answer. With Computer control on, it can also use websites, and on a Mac the apps you allow. It never uses a terminal or any app that runs commands, on a Mac or Windows, and none can be added.
Nothing costly gets finished without you

items: No text messages of its own, and no phone calls unless you switch Call businesses on, on the Setup tab under What it can do: then only to businesses, on your own Bland account, after you press Place the call on a card that shows the words first.

No spending unless you switch Buying on, under Computer control: then only at shops you list, up to amounts you set, after you tap Press it for me. Every add-on is included, so nothing inside Archie is for sale.
No sending on its own. An email or text reply goes out when you press Send, or at a time you set.
On a website, it stops before any press it could not undo (submit, pay, book, order, sign up, delete, cancel) and shows you the page. Tap Press it for me, or press it in the window.
No locks, thermostats, or cameras. It can switch only the lights and plugs you added to its list yourself.

body.text: Payment and wiring instructions

If an email, document, or message gives new or changed payment or wiring instructions, your agent is told never to pass them on, forward them, or act on them, even if you ask, and to tell you to confirm by phone at a number you already have, such as the title company's. Unlike the other limits here, this one is an instruction the AI follows, and an AI can get it wrong, so read anything about moving money yourself.
No looking around your network

Anything else on your home or office network (a storage drive, a server, another computer) is refused by address before the request leaves. Lights and plugs are reached only through the list you built.
The off switch is yours
Every agent has Switch on and Switch off at the top of its own page. Quit Archie and nothing runs: your agent is on this computer and on no other.
Ask for one of these and your agent says so in one line and offers the nearest thing it can do.

guides.title: What to say to your agent
guides.summary: First messages that get your agent doing something useful.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: “Hi” gets a friendly hello back and nothing more, because nothing was asked. Try these instead.
Start with a fact
Skills that keep a list start empty: Sports Follow with no teams has nothing to report. Tell it once:

items: “Follow Arsenal and the Warriors.”
“Netflix is 15.49 a month, next due on the 8th.”
“I take metformin twice a day, refill due the 20th.”
“My mom’s birthday is March 3.”

body.text: Ask for the thing itself
“Can you manage my calendar?” gets you a yes. “What have I got on Thursday?” gets you Thursday.
Say how to talk to you
Tell it once, like “Keep answers to two sentences unless I ask for more” or “Tell me when you’re not sure instead of guessing”.
If a reply is wrong or badly pitched, say so in the chat; that’s faster than editing anything in Archie.
Hand over one list

items: Give it one list to keep: tasks, bills, whatever you hold in your head.
That skill already messages you on a schedule; change the time or turn it off with the switch on its card.
After a week, ask yourself whether you stopped checking something.

guides.title: What you need to run Archie
guides.summary: Everything your agent needs to answer, including a computer that stays on.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: What you need

items: A Mac or Windows computer that stays on and plugged in. Your agent answers only while it is awake; the guide "Your agent stopped replying" shows how to stop it sleeping.

An Otian account and a plan, signed in through a browser window: $30 a month or $299 a year, or $59 a month or $599 a year with the AI included (then skip the next item). Switch or stop any time. New accounts start on free credits. That account is the only one on our side, and it holds your email address and which plan you're on. Never a conversation we can read.

An AI account with a key, from a company in the guide Picking your AI account. Your agent thinks with it, and you pay that company directly. With the free credits you need none on your first day. Groq is very cheap after that, but needs a card.
Internet on that computer: every reply is a round trip to the AI company. A cable from your router is steadier than Wi-Fi.
Optional: a chat app (Telegram, Discord, Slack, or Matrix; on a Mac, iMessage needs no account), to reach you on your phone. Without one, your agent answers in Archie's Chat tab.

body.text: When your agent can answer

Your agent runs on this computer, inside Archie. It answers only while the computer is awake, Archie is running, and the agent is started. Closing Archie’s window is fine; quitting Archie stops it. Nothing is lost while it is asleep.
What you don’t need

items: Any coding, or a terminal. Chat apps connect by pasting or scanning a code.
A server, or a cloud account of any kind.
A second computer, as long as yours can stay on.
Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus. Neither includes the key Archie asks for.

body.text: Checking that everything works
On your agent's Setup tab, the AI account row names your provider and the top button reads Switch off. Send a message in the Chat tab and an answer comes back.

guides.title: Your agent stopped replying
guides.summary: Five reasons an agent goes quiet, in the order to check them.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: 1. The computer is off or asleep

Your agent pauses when Archie closes or the computer sleeps. Nothing is lost, but a 7:30am briefing needs the computer awake then, or, after a routine was missed while it slept, the Wake this computer button on that routine's row, which wakes it before each routine from then on.
Only the computer has to stay awake; the screen can go dark. Change this once:

items: On a Mac: plug it in, open System Settings, then Battery, then Options, and turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping on power adapter when the display is off".
On Windows: plug it in, open Settings, then System, then Power & battery. Set the screen to turn off after a few minutes, and sleep to Never while plugged in.

body.text: Closing a laptop lid sleeps it by default, which is a separate setting:

items: On Windows: open Control Panel, then Power Options, then "Choose what closing the lid does", and set "When I close the lid" to "Do nothing" for Plugged in.
On a Mac: a closed lid sleeps it unless it is plugged in with an external display connected (clamshell mode). Otherwise macOS has no supported way to keep it awake shut, so leave the lid open.
Either way, leave it where it can shed heat, not in a drawer or under a cushion.

body.text: If this computer goes everywhere with you, the guide "Give your agent a computer that stays home" shows how to move your agent to one that doesn't.
2. The agent is switched off
Agents you left running come back with Archie, but one you stopped stays stopped and hears nothing. Check the button at the top of its page: it reads Switch on while the agent is off.
3. Your AI credit ran out
Your agent says the account is out of credit. Top up where you made the key; your AI account’s guide has the billing link.
4. Nobody has claimed the agent
A new agent replies only by asking for the six-digit claim code shown in Archie. Send that code in the chat and it’s yours.
5. Two agents share one bot
Archie won’t switch on a second agent on the same bot, since they would split the conversation. If Switch on fails with a message that mentions another agent, this is why.
Still quiet? Press Switch off and then Switch on at the top of its page, so it picks up any change made while it was running.

guides.title: Where your information goes
guides.summary: What stays on this computer, what goes to your AI company and to us, and how to turn each off.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: What stays on this computer

Your agents, what they know about you, your conversations, files, notes and lists are kept in Archie's folder here. Keys you paste sit in this computer's password store (Keychain on a Mac, Credential Manager on Windows), where we have no way to read them; each goes only to its own company.
What goes to your AI company

To answer you, your agent sends the AI company you connected your message, the recent conversation, what it knows about you, and what it read for you, such as an email, straight from this computer on your account. Web searches run on that company's servers.

Until you connect an AI account of your own, the AI is ours (the free trial's credits, or a plan with the AI included): each request passes through our server, which writes down what it cost, never what it said, keeps no copy, and sends it on to Anthropic. Your agent reads no email or texts on our AI. Connecting your own account stops this from your agent's next start.
What each AI company says about training
As of August 2026, in their own terms:

items: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Groq say what Archie sends them is not used for training.
Google (Gemini) and Mistral say the same of their paid tiers only. Their free tiers train on what you send.
xAI (Grok): we could not check its terms, so read them before you connect it.
DeepSeek's privacy policy says it trains on personal data and stores it in China.

body.text: Each policy is linked at https://otianai.com/trust/#providers
What Otian AI holds

items: Your email address, and whether you have a current plan.
Which version of the Terms you agreed to, and when.
Your Archie version and edition, Mac or Windows, and when it last checked in: one record, rewritten at most every six hours.
Crash and error reports: where our code broke, the error line, and for an add-on, its name and failing tool. Never what you wrote.
On our AI, what each request cost, and a scrambled one-way stamp of the computer and internet address that claimed free credits.
Second-factor sign-in records, invoices for any guided session, and any refused checkout (the account, the country, the amount).
Your address on our weekly letter's list, and whether it is switched on.
After a trial or plan ends: which of our three emails went to you, and whether you stopped them.

With phone access on, the messages between your computer and phone, sealed with a key we never receive. Unsealed: when each was left, which version of Archie left it, whether it was picked up, and your phone's name from pairing.
How many times each add-on was added, but not by whom.

body.text: Our trust page keeps the current list: https://otianai.com/trust/#what-we-hold

How long: your phone deletes each message once it reads it; your computer clears any it never came back for a day after the answer, the next time Archie runs. The rest are in the privacy policy: https://otianai.com/privacy-policy/#data-retention
Chat apps and your phone

In Telegram, Discord, Slack, or Matrix, what your agent says crosses that company's servers like any message there. iMessage (on a Mac only; Windows has none) is encrypted end to end by Apple. Archie Mobile, our phone app, locks each message with a key only your computer and phone hold, so we hold those messages and cannot read them. Phone access is off until you turn it on.
How to turn each one off
Settings and Account are at the bottom of the left sidebar.

items: An account or app: on your agent's Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files, or under Apps, press the trash can beside it. Its sign-in or key stays in Settings, under Saved keys, until you remove it there.

A chat app: on your agent's Setup tab, under Chat app, pick it and press Disconnect. Its token stays in Settings, under Saved keys, until you remove it there. Your agent still answers in the Archie window.
Your AI company: change it on your agent's Setup tab, under AI account.
Crash and error reports and the version check-in: in Settings, under Privacy, turn off Send crash reports.
Your phone, or a lost one: on your agent's Setup tab, under Chat app, press Archie Mobile, then Disconnect every phone. That empties the sealed mailbox too.

This computer: on the Account page, under Resetting Archie, press Reset Archie, then type reset. Your agents and saved keys are erased and every phone disconnected; Open Archie at login and waking this computer for routines stay.
Your Otian AI account, or the weekly letter: sign in at https://otianai.com/account/
Our emails after a trial or plan ends: press Stop these emails at the bottom of one.

body.text: This says what Archie does. It is not a compliance certification, and does not make Archie HIPAA or GDPR compliant: what you send still goes to an AI company.
A copy to print or send to someone: https://otianai.com/trust/where-your-information-goes/

guides.title: Letting other people in
guides.summary: Approve someone to message your agent, and know what they can do.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: Once claimed, your agent answers only you. Anyone else is told to ask you for access, and their message is dropped before it costs anything.
Two ways to let someone in

items: They message your agent, appear in Archie under “People waiting to message your agent”, and you press Approve.
Or press Add someone, and they send the code Archie shows to your agent in the chat app.

body.text: Either way they join as a Guest, with a Remove button beside them. An invite code works once, expires after a day, and Stop accepting this code ends it early.
Your agent tells you the first time someone new writes, once per person. Not now clears them and they can write again; Block silences them, even against an invite code.
What an approved person can do

cells: Message the agent and get answers
Read its memory, files, and records
Add to and change its lists (on “Talk and add to your lists” or “Everything you can”)
Act through it: send drafts, approve calendar changes (only on “Everything you can”)
Change how it works, or approve other people

body.text: Guests start on “Talk to your agent”, which cannot act on your accounts. On any of the three settings they read everything it holds, so approve people you would trust with that.
If something goes wrong

items: Each chat app keeps its own approved list. Only three things reset one: pasting a different connection code for that app, pressing Disconnect on it on the Setup tab under Chat app (which resets this agent only), or removing its saved code on the Settings page, under Saved keys (which resets every agent using it).
Someone got no reply: they are told once that they aren’t approved, then your agent stays quiet for about an hour. Approve them and ask them to write again.
Reset access makes the agent forget its owner and every guest, and issues a new code. It answers nobody until it is claimed again.

body.text: Your agent only replies while it’s started and Archie is running on this computer, so a silent agent is more often a closed laptop than a permissions problem.

guides.title: Telling your agent who it serves
guides.summary: Tell your agent your name, your work, and your house rules, with help if you’re stuck.
guides.author: Otian AI

body.text: An agent that knows nothing about you asks who Sam is every time and books the Friday you never work. Fix that once in the Who this agent serves box, on your agent’s Personality tab.
What to put in the box

items: Your name, and what you do.
What takes up most of your time.
Who it will hear about often: family, colleagues, clients.
House rules: anything it should always or never do.
For a business: the key people, and what matters most in how you work.

body.text: Help filling in the box

Press “Not sure what to write?” above the box, answer up to five short questions, and a draft lands in the box for you to change. Or let your agent ask: a newly claimed agent interviews you over chat and fills this in. “Redo introduction”, at the bottom of the Personality tab, starts that again.
Where this box ends up
It is handed to your agent with every message, and to every skill it hands work to. It saves as you type, and a running agent restarts a couple of seconds later to pick up the change.
Redo introduction replaces this box entirely, so copy anything you wrote by hand first. Memory is the other place facts live: what your agent worked out as you talked.
